name: ductus
description: Ductus integration engine: interface tests in the Test Explorer, run and debugged per test; validate's findings in Problems on save; debugging without launch.json; Deploy to dev; Promote… a release across your engines; each interface's history; a stored message debugged from the web UI.

ductus.path.markdownDescription: The `ductus` program the extension runs (tests, `validate`, debugging). Empty: `ductus` on the `PATH`, as a terminal finds it. A path relative to the workspace folder or with `${workspaceFolder}` works too. It must be 0.7.0 or newer.

ductus.environment.markdownDescription: The environment the project is read in for tests, `validate` and debugging (`--env`): `${NAME}` values come from `environments/<env>.yaml`.

ductus.validateOnSave.markdownDescription: Run `ductus validate` when a file of a project is saved (once for several saves close together) and show its findings in Problems. Off: only when the workspace opens and with **Ductus: Validate the project**.

ductus.deployToDevOnSave.markdownDescription: Deploy to dev when a file of a project is saved (once for several saves close together): the project's running `ductus dev` applies the folder in place, as **Ductus: Deploy to dev** does. Nothing happens while no `ductus dev` runs for the project. Off: only with the command.

ductus.engines.markdownDescription: The engines **Ductus: Promote…** deploys to and fetches releases from, by name: `{ "test": "https://ductus-test:7700", "prod": "https://ductus-prod:7700" }` (each its REST API, as `ductus deploy --to` takes it). Tokens aren't kept here: each is asked for the first time it's needed and kept in your system's keychain. Your own `ductus dev` needs no entry (**Deploy to dev** finds it).

commands.title: Choose where the history is read from

enumDescriptions: `ductus test --inspect`: the tests of the open file's interface
`ductus try --inspect`: the open file (a message, a fixture) through its interface
`ductus dev --inspect`: a dev engine with the open file's interface under the debugger

file.description: A file of the interface (try: the message). Default: the open file.

args.description: More options for the command, e.g. ["--filter", "A31"].
